_meta.purpose: Deterministic advisory lookup table: model_label + risk_level -> structured advisory.
how_to_use: 1. Look up the advisory by (model_label, risk_level) from the RiskAssessment output.
2. Render summary + immediate_actions + prevention + monitoring to the owner, in that order.
4. Evaluate global.environmental_modifiers against the weather_snapshot fields from the Risk Engine.
5. Render global.pesticide_safety_disclaimer whenever the advisory contains a chemical, drug, or dosage reference.
6. The AI prediction is not treated as veterinary confirmation. Expert confirmation is represented through the ExpertValidation workflow.

advisories.cause: Lumpy skin disease virus (LSDV, capripoxvirus), transmitted primarily by biting flies, mosquitoes, and ticks
advisories.source: ICAR-NIVEDI; DAHD, Government of India — LSD advisory; WOAH technical disease guidance

LOW.summary: Low vector activity currently indicated. Continue routine vaccination and monitoring.
immediate_actions: No immediate treatment needed.
prevention: Ensure all animals are vaccinated against LSD per the state schedule.
Keep animals in clean, dry shelters with minimal standing water nearby.
monitoring: Check animals weekly for skin nodules, fever, or reduced milk yield.

MODERATE.summary: Vector activity may be rising. Verify vaccination status across the herd.
immediate_actions: Check vaccination records — unvaccinated animals should be vaccinated promptly.
Reduce standing water and dung piles near animal shelters.
prevention: Use fly and tick control measures (pour-on, sprays) as advised by the local veterinary officer.
monitoring: Scout for early signs: fever, drooling, reduced appetite, skin nodules.

HIGH.summary: Conditions strongly favor LSD vector activity. Act promptly to protect the herd.
immediate_actions: Vaccinate any unvaccinated animals immediately.
Isolate animals showing early signs — fever, skin lumps, or milk drop.
Intensify vector control in and around the shelter.
prevention: Avoid moving animals to or from areas with active LSD reports.
Do not share equipment or vehicles between farms without disinfection.
monitoring: Check the herd daily for skin nodules and fever.

CRITICAL.summary: Very high LSD risk. Immediate veterinary action and strict biosecurity required.
immediate_actions: Contact the nearest veterinary officer immediately — LSD is a notifiable disease.
Isolate suspected cases in a separate shelter with dedicated handlers.
Halt all animal movement from the premises until confirmed.
prevention: Disinfect vehicles, equipment, and footwear entering the premises.
Notify neighboring farms and the local veterinary dispensary.
monitoring: Check the entire herd twice daily for new cases.

advisories.cause: Foot-and-mouth disease virus (FMDV, Aphthovirus), highly contagious among cloven-hoofed animals
advisories.source: DAHD FMD Control Programme; ICAR-IVRI; WOAH FMD technical guidance

LOW.summary: Low current risk. Maintain routine FMD vaccination per the national programme.
immediate_actions: No immediate action needed.
prevention: Follow the six-monthly FMD vaccination schedule.
Maintain clean, dry shelters and footbaths at entry points.
monitoring: Check animals weekly for mouth or hoof lesions, drooling, or lameness.

MODERATE.summary: Cool, moist conditions may aid FMD virus survival in the environment. Verify vaccination status.
immediate_actions: Verify vaccination records — booster doses are critical.
Restrict visitors and vehicles from entering animal areas.
prevention: Disinfect footwear and equipment at entry points.
Avoid introducing new animals without a 14-day quarantine.
monitoring: Check animals daily for blisters on mouth, tongue, and hooves.

HIGH.summary: Elevated FMD risk. Strict biosecurity and vaccination compliance required.
immediate_actions: Vaccinate any animal overdue for a booster.
Isolate any animal showing lameness, drooling, or fever immediately.
Report suspected cases to the local veterinary officer.
prevention: Halt all animal movement until the situation is assessed.
Disinfect pens, feeding troughs, and watering points.
monitoring: Check the herd twice daily for early signs.

CRITICAL.summary: Very high FMD risk. Immediate veterinary notification required — FMD is a notifiable disease.
immediate_actions: Contact the veterinary officer immediately.
Stop all animal movement — no animals in or out.
Isolate infected and in-contact animals.
prevention: Disinfect everything leaving the premises — vehicles, equipment, personnel.
Notify neighboring farms and the local dispensary.
monitoring: Check all animals twice daily for new lesions.

advisories.cause: Bacterial infection of the hoof and interdigital skin, favored by prolonged wet, muddy conditions
advisories.source: ICAR-IVRI extension guidance; state veterinary department guidelines

LOW.summary: Dry conditions — low risk of foot infection. Continue routine hoof inspection.
immediate_actions: No treatment needed.
prevention: Keep shelters dry and bedding clean.
Inspect hooves monthly for cracks or early lesions.
monitoring: Watch for lameness during routine handling.

MODERATE.summary: Wet conditions forming. Take preventive hoof-care steps now.
immediate_actions: Clean and dry shelters; replace wet bedding.
Check hooves of any lame animal.
prevention: Use a footbath with copper sulfate or zinc sulfate solution at entry points.
monitoring: Inspect hooves weekly for softening or early lesions.

HIGH.summary: Prolonged wet conditions favor foot infections. Prompt action needed.
immediate_actions: Move animals to dry ground or a raised, dry shelter.
Footbath all animals; separate and inspect any showing lameness.
Trim overgrown hooves to reduce trapping of mud and bacteria.
prevention: Improve drainage around shelters and watering points.
Avoid standing water where animals gather.
monitoring: Check for lameness and hoof swelling daily.

CRITICAL.summary: Severe foot-infection risk under extended wet conditions. Veterinary treatment likely required.
immediate_actions: Contact the veterinary officer for suspected cases.
Isolate severely affected animals to prevent spread.
Clean and dress affected hooves under veterinary guidance.
prevention: Rebuild or relocate shelters to higher, drier ground.
Disinfect footbath areas daily.
monitoring: Check all animals twice daily for new lameness.

LOW.summary: Animal appears healthy. Good time to reinforce preventive practices.
immediate_actions: No action needed.
prevention: Maintain the current vaccination, feeding, and shelter schedule.
Continue routine observation — early detection is cheaper than late treatment.
monitoring: Re-check in 1-2 weeks or after any notable weather change.

MODERATE.summary: Animal appears healthy; environmental conditions are shifting. Double-check preventive practices.
immediate_actions: No action needed.
prevention: Review shelter drainage and bedding as conditions change.
Continue routine herd observation.

HIGH.summary: Animal appears healthy despite conditions favoring disease. Maintain preventive discipline.
immediate_actions: No action needed.
prevention: Maintain strict sanitation, vaccination, and vector control while conditions remain elevated.
monitoring: Observe the herd more frequently — approximately every 3-4 days.

CRITICAL.summary: Animal appears healthy despite high environmental favorability for disease. Stay vigilant.
immediate_actions: No action needed for this animal.
prevention: Maintain strict biosecurity and vector control across the herd.

global.low_confidence_note: AI classification confidence for this report was below 70%. Treat the condition label as provisional. We recommend a clearer follow-up photo, or a veterinary review, before acting on this advisory — especially before any medication or treatment.
global.pesticide_safety_disclaimer: Drug and dosage references in this advisory data are drawn from veterinary extension sources describing practices applicable at the time of writing. Approved uses, formulations, and withdrawal periods can change and may vary by state. Verify the current product label and applicable registration before administering any drug or treatment to livestock. Consult a registered veterinary practitioner.

environmental_modifiers.note: High wind detected — delay any spray or pour-on application to reduce drift and poor coverage.
A narrow dewpoint spread indicates very high atmospheric moisture. This favors fly and tick activity (vector risk) and aids virus survival on surfaces.
Sustained high cloud cover can reduce daytime heat and keep shelters humid — conditions that favor vector resting and virus survival.
High soil moisture indicates waterlogged or muddy ground — the primary driver of foot infections in cattle.
